GoogleDeepMind
Oct 15th, 2026
At the Limits of Computability: Steps Towards
Autonomous AI Discovery on the Busy Beaver
Frontier
Marco Dos Santosl.2, Vivek Veeriah', Alex Havrilla', Andrew Bolt', Goran Zuzic', Satinder Singh' and Tom
Zahavy'. 1 Google DeepMind, 2 University of Cambridge. Work done at Google DeepMind.
Recent breakthroughs in AI for mathematics—ranging from Olympiad medal performances to resolving
long-standing open conjectures—have rapidly expanded what automated systems can achieve. Yet these
successes primarily concern predefined, human-formulated problems, leaving open how AI systems can
autonomously uncover mathematical structure and formulate new questions. To push beyond static
challenges, we explore the Busy Beaver (BB) domain, an uncomputable frontier that is fundamentally
provides a natural setting for sustained exploration through mathematical conjecture and proof. In
this paper, we introduce a Gemini-based agentic pipeline that automatically discovers accelerations of
Turing machines, expressed as compact mathematical rules summarizing many execution steps. Our
system integrates pattern recognition, automated conjecturing, informal mathematical reasoning, and
formal theorem proving in Lean. with this framework, our system autonomously discovered and formally
verified novel Collatz-like accelerations for eleven machines in BB(6). Subject to community acceptance,
we provisionally classify these machines as Cryptids, namely machines whose blank-tape executions
admit exact, compact mathematical descriptions but whose halting behavior remains unresolved. These
results advance the analysis of BB(6) holdouts on the Busy Beaver frontier and demonstrate the potential
of autonomous AI systems for open-ended mathematical discovery in fundamental computer science.
